claims.text: Replacing full thermodynamic integration with an MLP-based perturbation scheme will yield accurate free-energy differences for Ta-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Accuracy requires the MLP training set to include configurations with high lattice distortion and local chemical ordering.
The initial material is a solid Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy with high configurational entropy and significant lattice distortion.
Standard experimental melting data are unavailable for the target alloy.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the target alloy's complex liquid structure.
Ab initio full thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive under the stated throughput constraints.
A perturbation or free-energy-perturbation calculation using an MLP can bypass full phase-space thermodynamic integration.
Training on high-temperature liquid and solid configurations allows the MLP to capture local chemical ordering and lattice-distortion patterns in both phases.
Standard EAM and Lennard-Jones potentials miss the relevant local chemical ordering and lattice-distortion patterns.
The MLP learns complex nonlinear interactions governing liquid structure and the solid-liquid interface in multicomponent alloys.
Learning these interactions allows perturbation theory to estimate solid-liquid free-energy differences accurately without sampling the entire phase space.
Lennard-Jones-only potentials can produce unreliable predictions in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed scheme will predict melting temperatures and free-energy differences within 5% of experimental or high-fidelity ab initio benchmarks.
The proposed scheme will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude relative to full thermodynamic integration.
Omitting high-temperature liquid data from the training set will cause unreliable predictions.
The hypothesis fails if phase separation is driven by mixing enthalpies that are not represented in the training data.
Chromium can promote the phase separation identified as a boundary condition.
An MLP may not generalize to extreme lattice distortion and high-temperature disorder without explicit high-energy liquid configurations in its training set.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that adding high-temperature liquid and distorted configurations should make Model 2 accurate, and the predicted outcome sets a less-than-5% target. The falsification rule nevertheless labels the combination of Model 1 exceeding 10% error and Model 2 remaining below 5% error as falsification, even though that result supports the stated hypothesis.
